title: What If Europe's Most Dangerous Supervolcano Erupted?

scenes.text: What if Campi Flegrei erupted? Half a million people live in the danger zone.
It sits under Naples, in a caldera about 14 kilometers wide, a third of it below the bay.
Its biggest eruption, about 39,000 years ago, spread ash over much of Europe and parts of Russia.
The ground there has risen about 4.6 feet since 2005. A new eruption would likely be much smaller.
Even so, pyroclastic flows could race at 30 to 60 miles an hour and reach about 800 degrees Celsius.
The ash could disrupt flights across Europe. Scientists say the current unrest does not mean an eruption is near.
